title: Using SRC layout without building a package
author: jksjieij
barry-scott
text: You put all the source in src including the __main__.py.

author: lverweijen
text:
You should put your__main__.pyin “src/pkg/”.
Instead of the workaround, you can also install it using:
pip install --editable .

Often, you can also do a cd srcbefore running the code.

author: barry-scott
text:
As an example of a small project:
$ tree ssh_wait
ssh_wait
├── LICENSE
├── pyproject.toml
├── README.md
├── run-test.sh
└── src
    └── ssh_wait
        ├── __init__.py
        └── __main__.py

author: jksjieij
text:
Based on the feedback and Barry’s answer you can do it in multiple ways:
PYTHONPATH=./src python3 -m <pkg>_me
python3 -m src.<pkg>_me
pip install -e $PWD
cd ./src; python3 -m <pkg>_me

Regarding the “workaround” in the User Guide, I’m not sure how useful it is to use it!
